summary: Frozen terminal, navigation, identity, discovery, error, and provenance baseline completed for four exact Paper revisions across 32 width/profile cells plus machine CLI/API and deployed-contract probes. The measurement assignment passed reproducibility, while the current readers and contracts fail multiple predeclared hard thresholds.

commands_or_probes: bp paper view --profile ansi256 --width {20,40,80,120} for four exact revision pins
bp paper view --profile none --width {20,40,80,120} for four exact revision pins
bp doc get for four exact revision pins
bp doc history --limit 1 for four Papers
bp paper view missing-paper typed-error control
GET /papers/{slug}/source with Accept application/json, text/html, and text/plain

observed_facts: All 32 declared terminal cells were captured from the four exact revision pins; ANSI256 renders contained ANSI escapes and NoColor renders did not.
ANSI-stripped Unicode-codepoint width measurement found zero lines beyond the requested widths.
At width 20 the eight render cells expanded to 72242 total lines; the largest single cell was CCH28 at 13111 lines. Totals declined to 28662, 13278, and 8964 at widths 40, 80, and 120.
The two terminal surfaces had identical aggregate line counts, 61573 each; heading text matched in 558/580 repeated comparisons on each surface.
No render cell exposed a structural header carrier, explicit tone label, or pinned revision carrier.
Paper view help exposed width selection but no outline, pager, or history option.
Source marks contained zero structured task links; three textual task-like tokens were present.
A requested history limit of 1 returned 14, 10, 12, and 12 records for CCH29, PDS45, CCH28, and PDS44 respectively.
History identities were UUIDs and none equaled the current document _rev hash.
The missing-Paper CLI control exited 4 and retained both not_found and request_id text.
For all four deployed Paper source endpoints, Accept application/json and text/plain returned 406 while Accept text/html returned 200 with an application/json body.
No deployed Paper source response exposed an ETag. The capabilities endpoint returned 200 with ETag W/"caps-67eb1a68b92f197b" and a request-id header; Paper schema discovery returned 200.
Missing public/source HTTP probes with JSON or text Accept headers returned negotiation-level 406 responses with request IDs rather than an identity-level typed 404.
inferences: Width containment does not compensate for severe vertical line expansion, absent navigation, or loss of semantic carriers.
A textual task token is not equivalent to a navigable task relationship.
Document _rev hashes and history UUIDs are distinct identity domains and should be labeled separately.
The deployed source endpoint's media-type behavior makes machine discovery fragile even though capabilities and schema discovery themselves succeed.
recommendations: Treat this as the frozen pre-candidate baseline for later candidate comparisons; do not select a final format from E03 alone.
Require explicit non-color hierarchy/header/tone/revision carriers and structured task linkage in any candidate.
Require bounded paging/outline/history navigation and prove limit forwarding before a candidate can pass.
Normalize source content negotiation, typed missing-resource errors, ETag or equivalent immutable attestation, and request-id behavior across media types.
unresolved_unknowns: Unicode codepoint counts are a conservative reproducible proxy, not a full wcwidth measurement for every terminal and glyph.
The deployed-contract snapshot is time-bound and may change independently of the frozen local artifacts.
Studio and real-mail-reader behavior are outside E03 and are neither passed nor failed here.

validation.independent_leader_replay: PASS twice with 253 checks and the identical artifact-set SHA

risks: Transient deployed 5xx responses were retried with bounded attempts during capture; raw stable artifacts record only the decisive responses.
Aggregate repeated-cell semantic scores are diagnostic baselines and must not be mistaken for unique source-node denominators.
